This action would not replace the trout habitat lost, however, as the project would cause a complete loss of trout stream waters in the area inundated. Trout streams are a limited resource in South Carolina. Trout Unlimited, in its letter of comment, indicated that the State's trout streams are now limited to about 250 miles, much of which is considered marginal.
Reductions of coldwater habitat in Lake Jocassee (Section 3.2.2.3) would have an adverse impact on the two-story fishery, stated by SCWMRD to be, "... The only acceptable compensation for the loss of nearly one-forth of the trout streams in this State to the construction of Lake Jocassee" (Timmerman, 1976). Applicant has not proposed any measures to mitigate for possible fishery losses resulting from reduction of coldwater habitat in Lake Jocassee through project operation, or entrainment losses. The Exhibit W indicates (pg. 4-1) that adequate compensatory action would be taken to enhance the environmental quality of the region in areas where adverse environmental aspects cannot be avoided or mitigated.
One possible measure that Applicant could take to mitigate losses to the Lake Jocassee fishery would be to assist the SCWMRD in their stocking program at Lake Jocassee. Such a program could be especially beneficial if, at some time in the future, habitat changes in the lake require a change from management as a carry-over fishery (stocked fish surviving for more than one season) to management as a put-and-take fishery. Such a change might require increased stocking rates to maintain an equivalent sport fishery to that now existing.
Reduction in coldwater habitat in Lake Jocassee could be offset in the future by reduced productivity as the reservoir ages and stabilizes. Continued monitoring of water quality and the fishery resources of Lake Jocassee would be necessary to fully assess the degree of habitat reduction and impact of project operation on the trout fishery.
The Exhibit H of the Bad Creek application states that the operation of several pumped storage projects using Lake Jocassee as the lower reservoir are comtemplated for the future. Additional steam generation capacity is also contemplated, in association with Lake Keowee.
